checked.found: Pixii built a hand-cranked magneto-electric machine in 1832; Ampere suggested the commutator (first commutated dynamo).

Siemens discovered the dynamo-electric principle and built the machine in 1866, reported to the Berlin Academy early 1867. Wheatstone and Varley were near-simultaneous, but Siemens is the usual credit.

Godalming supply began September/October 1881, driven by a waterwheel at Westbrook Mill on the Wey, widely called the world's first public electricity supply (not permanent; abandoned c.1884). Name is exactly 35 chars.
Pearl Street began serving customers 4 September 1882 through underground conductors.
Westinghouse won the lighting contract for the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition with an AC system.
Ginori Conti's test on 4 July 1904 lit four or five bulbs from a steam-driven dynamo (a demonstration; the plant came 1911-13).

Sources split: 132kV grid constructed 1927-33, began operating as interconnected regional grids 1933, ran as a single integrated unit from 1938; National Grid's own page gives no year for commercial operation. 1935 not confirmed. 'World's first integrated national network' is supported by National Grid's history page.
1.25 MW turbine on Grandpa's Knob first synchronized to the Central Vermont grid on 19 October 1941; first megawatt-scale turbine (Denmark's 1919 Buddinge turbine was far smaller).
PG&E Unit 1 (11 MW) began commercial operation 25 September 1960; ASME calls it the first commercial geothermal electric station in North America.
9 November 1965; improperly set protective relay on a line at Sir Adam Beck station, Ontario, started the cascade; about 30 million affected.
First turbine on grid August 1966, inaugurated November 1966; world's first large-scale tidal plant.
PDCI energized in 1970 (Celilo, Oregon to Sylmar near Los Angeles); first major US HVDC link.
Opened/commissioned 1984 inside Elidir mountain; full output within about 16 seconds.
13 March 1989 geomagnetic storm collapsed Hydro-Quebec's grid in about 90 seconds; about 6 million without power.
Prius went on sale in Japan 10 December 1997; described as the first mass-produced hybrid car.
14 August 2003; FirstEnergy 345kV line in northern Ohio tripped on tree contact, cascade blacked out 50 million in the US Northeast and Ontario.
Production and first deliveries began early 2008 (first car February 2008, 27 customers by September 2008); pack of 6,831 laptop-style lithium-ion cells.
Powerwall announced 30 April 2015 for load shifting, backup power and solar self-consumption.

Year 2017 correct (plugged in 1 December 2017, then the largest lithium-ion battery). But sources say 100 days was Tesla's deadline; it was delivered in about 60-63 days after the grid agreement was signed, so 'built in about 100 days' is inaccurate.
checked.suggestion: The world's biggest lithium-ion battery at the time began stabilising South Australia's grid, built in under 100 days.
